hypothesis: A positive pair with more than q distinct projections must belong to different factors when every local factor language has at most q words. A complete k-partite graph of such pairs fixes a unique known-k partition, subject to direct full-block cap and negative checks.
motivation: Relax the singleton-language assumption without unsoundly importing its variation threshold of one into the q=2 class; avoid exhaustive search on a sufficient-coverage family.
assumptions: known k nonempty disjoint alphabet blocks
finite local languages of cardinality at most q
nonempty positive evidence for the recovery certificate
critical_guard: Pair cardinalities are necessary constraints, not sufficient positive feasibility for q>=2; full candidate projection languages must be checked.
candidate_coverage: Equal-size blocks; repeated local words; forward block order, reverse block order, lockstep interleaving; add a fourth positive with second local words. Only a proposed family until independently generated and checked.
experiment_gate: No stage2 provider execution before stage1 serial timing ends and master go.
